title: 5-HTTLPR × stress and depression: collaborative meta-analysis finds no broadly generalizable interaction
summary: A focused negative-result / replication-synthesis record for the famous 5-HTTLPR × stress depression interaction. The record encodes the collaborative meta-analysis as a boundary-sensitive nonconfirmation, not as denial that stress affects depression or that G×E can exist.

status_history.note: The seed flags candidate-gene psychiatric genetics and serotonin-theory overstatement as relevant missing-half material.
Promoted in rev0018 candidate-gene / GWAS denominator lane.

time.claim_origin_context: interaction hypothesis first proposed in 2003 per source abstract

place.scope: European-ancestry collaborative meta-analysis of depression/stress/5-HTTLPR datasets

subjects.name: stressful life events / childhood maltreatment broad and narrow definitions

claims.claim: Culverhouse et al. describe a collaborative meta-analysis of the 5-HTTLPR × stress depression hypothesis using 31 datasets containing 38,802 European-ancestry subjects, with uniform data-analysis scripts implementing a protocol.
what_would_change_status: A corrected source changes the dataset count, ancestry scope, sample size, or protocol/uniform-analysis description.

claims.claim: The collaborative meta-analysis reports no support for the interaction hypothesis: no subgroup or variable definition produced a statistically significant 5-HTTLPR × stress interaction, while life stressors showed strong main-effect risk and 5-HTTLPR genotype did not.
what_would_change_status: A later collaborative meta-analysis with comparable or superior denominator control finds a robust broadly generalizable interaction.

claims.claim: The record’s status is boundary-sensitive: the source conclusion leaves room for modest effects observable only in limited situations, so the cube should not encode the claim as “G×E impossible” or “stress does not matter.”
what_would_change_status: A future review shows the boundary caution is either too weak or unnecessary for current consensus.
